A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TR scheduling research. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and equations, figures, tables, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and object-detection experiments, training analyses, and controlled comparisons of TR settings and update schemes.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and supplementary analyses and adds ImageNet results for quantized DeiT-T/S models in Table 3.

M1.justification: Transition counting, running-TR estimation, TALR adjustment, and latent-weight updates remain unchanged in Equations (5) and (10)-(12) and Algorithm 1. The quantization schemes move to supplement D.1 without substantive changes. Coupling the scheduler with AdamW was already evaluated in v1 Table 7.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet classification and MS COCO detection. DeiT-T/S adds model configurations within the existing ImageNet task, without changing datasets, represented populations, or input scenarios. Detection results moved to the supplement remain present.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 introduces AdamW as the comparator for ImageNet DeiT-T/S experiments; v1's ImageNet comparisons used SGD and Adam. AdamW's earlier CIFAR-100 comparison remains in supplement Table E. The published QAT comparator set in v1 Table 3 is retained in v2 Table A; newly cited pseudo-quantization methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds DeiT-T/S evaluation at 2- and 3-bit precision using AdamW/AdamWT. Table G specifies 300 epochs, batch size 256, learning rate 3e-4, weight decay 5e-2, and cosine scheduling. These are settings for new experiments; the previously reported CNN and detection settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The step-scheduler comparisons, initial/final TR analyses, optimizer comparisons, TALR update variants, training curves, and detection case studies are retained in supplement A-C. Duplicating v1 Figure 5 as v2 Figure 3 and Figure C adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: v1 Table 8 and v2 Table F report identical means and standard deviations over five random runs. The added DeiT results introduce no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 3 adds DeiT results: AdamW/AdamWT achieve 54.6/57.4 and 68.1/69.5 for 2-/3-bit DeiT-T, and 68.4/71.8 and 77.6/78.5 for DeiT-S. These are new architecture results, not revisions of earlier scores. All numerical entries in v1 Tables 1-8 are retained in corresponding v2 tables.

T1.justification: The TR definition, effective-step-size derivation and assumptions, quantizer formulas, and alternative TALR update equations remain mathematically unchanged. Material moves between the main paper and supplement and receives different equation numbers; no new proofs or formal assumptions are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about shortcomings of LR scheduling, the proposed TR/TALR approach, and its generality and effectiveness. Adding DeiT evidence supports the existing generality claim without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 Section 2 adds an explanation that directly controlling quantized-weight changes avoids the training/inference discrepancy attributed to pseudo-quantization noise methods. Existing interpretations of convergence, latent-weight distributions, TR tuning, and layer-dependent effective-step-size targets are retained.

D1.justification: Supplement D.2 and Table G document initialization and hyperparameters for the new DeiT experiments while retaining existing implementation details. v1's explicit project-site link is removed; v2 instead promises future online code availability without a link. This changes access information without establishing any change in actual online availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DeiT reference and three pseudo-quantization works, including NIPQ. A new related-work paragraph contrasts their noise-based training, inference discrepancy, and additional remedies with TR scheduling. The existing positioning against QAT methods and binary-network optimizers remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the paper into a shorter main text and supplement A-E, moving quantization schemes, implementation settings, state-of-the-art comparisons, and most analyses and discussion. Much prose is retained, but the narrative structure changes extensively. Author order, affiliations, and contribution notes also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and extensively relocates displays. It splits the detection table, adds the DeiT table and hyperparameter rows, and duplicates the TR-analysis figure in the main text and supplement. Figure E also introduces incorrect equation labels in its legends: (v)/(vi) instead of the variants numbered (i)/(ii).

improvement.justification: The added DeiT-T/S results and reported training settings provide a useful test of the generality claimed in v1 beyond CNNs, while the pseudo-quantization discussion updates the context. These limited gains outweigh presentation and access-information regressions, including removal of the project link, the ResNet-50 discussion pointing to Table B, and Figure E's inconsistent equation labels. The core method and prior evidence remain intact.
